name: Desmopressin
executiveSummary: Vasopressin analogue. Adult DI: **1–2 µg IV/SC every 12–24 h** (or nasal/PO). Hemophilia A / von Willebrand: **0.3 µg/kg IV** over 15–30 min. Hyponatremia risk — fluid restrict.
indications:
## Indications

- Central diabetes insipidus.
- Mild hemophilia A and selected von Willebrand disease peri-procedure.
- Nocturnal enuresis (PO/nasal) in >6 years per specialist.

## Precautions

- **Water intoxication / hyponatremia** — restrict fluids, check Na+.
- Not in von Willebrand type 2B. Avoid in severe renal failure / HF with retention.
- Nasal/PO/IV formulations are **not 1:1 interchangeable**.

> Refrigerate ampoules/nasal solution (2–8 °C) per label.

adulto.presentation: Ampoule 4 µg/mL; nasal spray/solution; tabs 0.1–0.2 mg.
adulto.dose: DI: **1–2 µg IV or SC** every 12–24 h (titrate); nasal/PO by response. Hemophilia/vWD: **0.3 µg/kg IV** 30 min before procedure. Enuresis: PO **0.2–0.4 mg** at bedtime (specialist).
adulto.administration: IV: dilute (~0.1 µg/mL) in NS/D5W; **15–30 min**. Slow SC. Nasal on anterior mucosa.
adulto.notes: Potentiated by carbamazepine, NSAIDs, SSRIs/TCAs (↓ Na+).

pediatrico.presentation: Ampoule 4 µg/mL; nasal 0.1 mg/mL; tabs 0.1–0.2 mg.
pediatrico.dose: DI IV/SC: **2–4 µg/day** divided every 12 h (titrate). Nasal: **5–10 µg** (0.05–0.1 mL) twice daily. PO <12 years: start **0.05 mg q12h** (range **0.1–0.8 mg/day**); ≥12 years up to **1.2 mg/day**. Hemophilia/vWD ≥3 months: **0.3 µg/kg IV**. Enuresis ≥6 years: nasal **10–40 µg** or PO ≥12 years **0.2–0.4 mg** nightly.

neonatal.dose: Orientative DI: **0.1–0.3 µg/kg** IV per protocol.

stability:
## Stability

- Refrigerate ampoules and nasal per label.
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Headache, nausea, hyponatremia, fluid retention, flushing; rare thrombosis (hemostatic doses).
